trigger: holder of global NetworkElement:Read (any authenticated session under RBAC-off, auth_routes.cpp:846) calls get_network_element_state on /network-instances/*/fdb
summary: Internal contradiction: 'a confined operator ... never a switch's whole table' vs D5/D10 serving raw FDB/ARP subtrees on the global unconfined Read via cache-Get; RBAC-off audience (every Read admitted) unstated; floor-vs-no-floor undecided.
classification_rationale: ADR text contradicts its own D5/D10 and the legacy branch of require_permission

trigger: admin cookie session under RBAC-off, or any JIT-elevated session, calls GET /api/v1/network-elements/collector-targets
summary: 'a caller that is not a collector principal is denied' is false under require_permission: elevated sessions short-circuit (auth_routes.cpp:660), admin admitted for non-Read ops with RBAC off (:846); engine principals 403 under RBAC-off (:680) so the connector REQUIRES RBAC enabled — precondition unstated.
classification_rationale: false assurance against require_permission's branch order

trigger: admin grants a custom all-permission role to engine:netcollector
summary: Cited mitigation does not exist: validate_assignment (rbac_store.cpp:2079-2084) rejects only the literal admin role names; wildcard-equivalent custom roles are auditor-detected, not prevented. Derived HIGH via I6(a) false assurance; reporter's native MEDIUM disagreed.
classification_rationale: ADR cites a control the code does not implement

trigger: gnmic's device-side subscription (its own config, not core's) includes a config container; operator Gets an allowlisted root
summary: 'config-tree disclosure is structurally impossible' is false: gnmic's cache holds what gnmic subscribed from devices (gnmic config, which Yuzu does not write), gNMI Subscribe has no type filter, and allowlisted roots contain config containers (…/bgp/neighbors/neighbor/config/auth-password). D11 overrides vs D10 one-table rule also unstated.
classification_rationale: structural claim not supported by gNMI/gnmic semantics

trigger: in-purview individual read via MCP, a dashboard fragment, or a post-read audit site
summary: emit_behavioral_audit cannot be the DENY point as written: it is the HTTP wrapper returning a persist bool (rest_audit.hpp:206-219); MCP wraps the kernel itself; HTML/MCP ignore false by design; several sites audit AFTER the read; audit-off returns true. Also cited by ADR-0068 D5 and CONTEXT.md Purview.
classification_rationale: enforcement point named is an audit wrapper, not a gate

trigger: an admin opens and approves their own Incident
summary: 'four-eyes or admin' contradicts accepted ADR-0033 §4 (requester ≠ approver, distinct human roots, MFA step-up, Approve on the securable). If read as self-approval it violates an accepted ADR's normative requirement (policy-floor candidate); the Incident securable carrying Approve is unnamed.

trigger: per-target decrypt failure; audit-persist failure on the collector-targets route; body reaching a log
summary: D6 residual risk incomplete and ADR-3005 miscited (3005 is strictly write-only, no exception). Missing per ADR-0010: never-empty-secret on decrypt failure, generic error + audit + metric, fail-closed on audit-persist failure, body never logged (60s poll), bearer lifetime/rotation.
classification_rationale: ADR-0010 obligations the D6 contract must state (routed-concern 'Server storage substrate' row: security-guardian on any secret-at-rest) — recorder's derivation: no control fails today (design-only), so the fact is a missing required statement (I7, SHOULD), not I1; reporter's native MEDIUM agrees with the band

trigger: unresolved
summary: Verdict wording 'collection from an external source' could be read to admit vuln/threat-intel feeds, which ADR-1005:47 keeps in engine territory.

trigger: unresolved
summary: Interlock tripwire re-run CLOSED; no engine-path marker applies; D4 Set / Incident approval route through ADR-0033 §4/§10 primitives that are design-only today — precondition on those future ADRs, not this one.

trigger: ADR-0067/0068 merged under the standing acceptance convention
summary: Acceptance gate recorded only in a blockquote, not frontmatter/Binding-status as docs/agents/domain.md requires; ADR-0068 'binds on acceptance (merge)' while depending on a proposed ADR. Truth candidate for architect to size.

trigger: unresolved
summary: Routed-concern row deferred to slice 1 is a legitimate deferral (required-doc item 4 applies when the store/route/gate ships; item 6 names no obligation for ADR-only files).

trigger: unresolved
summary: Bare ADR-0031 (lines 6,139) and ADR-0016 (lines 7,169) cites; README requires the two collided numbers be cited by filename.

trigger: unresolved
summary: Glossary terms defined by mechanism (Network collector names gnmic/sidecar/flows; Collector principal names NetworkElement:Collect/single route/memory-only; Network element carries ADR-0033 §10/#1398 plumbing); Incident is a generic word — qualify as purview incident.

trigger: unresolved
summary: Nine lines >100 cols across the two ADRs; roadmap banner duplicates the ADR-1005 appendix verdict in full (drift risk).

trigger: unresolved
summary: Market-check paragraph cites external products/versions without sources; no ADR convention requires them; optional Sources list.

policy_floor: accepted ADR normative requirement: ADR-0031 Decision 8 'Every seam is a versioned contract. The seam inventory is normative' (0031:267-268) — core → gnmic is a new southbound seam B7 does not cover and ADR-0068 does not register it
trigger: ADR-0068 merged as written
summary: New seam core → network collector not registered in ADR-0031's normative seam inventory; the Considered-and-rejected rationale for a Yuzu-written collector ('a new seam ADR-0031's inventory lacks') is false because gnmic needs the identical seam. Fix: Consequences adds 'ADR-0031 D8 amended with B8 core → network collector' (contract: pinned image digest + D10 table + read-only); gnmic→core pull is B4-shaped; rewrite the rationale.
classification_rationale: rejection rationale contradicts the chosen design; plus absence of the seam registration an accepted ADR requires

trigger: two or more core replicas; Prometheus scrapes a non-leader
summary: yuzu_network_element_collector_stream_up described as 'pre-seeded' 0/1 under an absent-not-zero umbrella, with an alert on ==0: on a FencedLeaderOnly job a pre-seeded process gauge reads 0 on every non-leader forever (observability-conventions.md:16 requires dormancy = structural absence). last_fetch_seconds is per-replica too. Fix: leader-emitted only, present while leading, cleared on loss.
classification_rationale: internal contradiction (pre-seeded vs absent-not-zero) and vs the emission-posture convention; E6 cap NOT applied — the single-replica contract is a deployment gate, not proof the outcome cannot occur

trigger: implementing D7's read-time join verbatim
summary: Join path names two query surfaces that do not exist: FleetTopologyStore's ip_owner_ is private (public accessors are agent→IP only, in-memory, per-replica, 60s, TAR-pushing agents only); device_ci MACs are comma-joined TEXT with no by-value query; ADR-0012 §3 forbids a cross-schema method on NetworkElementStore. Fix: name a dedicated query owner, add a by-value MAC index/table, state the IP half is best-effort and an unresolved host reports 'unresolved'. discovered_devices link = soft id reference, v2 migration under the ADR-0012 runner.
classification_rationale: ADR names APIs the code does not expose

trigger: implementing D11 verbatim
summary: Vendoring gnmi protos into yuzu_proto as written fails Tier-1 buf lint (PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH on package gnmi under third_party/), buf breaking would police upstream changes on every pin bump, gen_proto.py flattens only yuzu/ includes (gnmi_ext import path), and 'nothing added to the agent' rests on static-archive elision. Fix: separate yuzu_gnmi_proto target linked by server/core only; buf lint/breaking ignore for third_party/; vendor at the canonical import path or record the rewrite; note the #572 shape for server tests.
classification_rationale: 'same library, no new linkage' claim contradicts the build's lint/flatten constraints

trigger: leadership loss while the Subscribe stream is open
summary: leader_gate.hpp is a per-tick attempt gate; a long-lived stream has no tick. ADR must state: subscribe only while leading, tear down on leadership loss (else two live subscriptions against gnmic's max-subscriptions and silently dropped fenced-out batches), honour epoch_fence_sql's isolation contract (leader_elector.hpp:153-158).
classification_rationale: required behaviour for the FencedLeaderOnly class not stated; routed row (fenced leader) names the header banners as the contract

trigger: unresolved
summary: 'use-case engine (consumes facts, never collects them)' contradicts ADR-1005:79/92 (first module ingests external vulnerability feeds); with the appendix row it would place feed collection in core. Fix (also sizes sec-8): appendix adds 'an estate fact is a fact about the customer's own estate; external domain data stays engine territory'; glossary → 'never collects estate facts'; roadmap:1109 'keeps the in-server shape' → 'control plane in core; data plane may be an external process'.
classification_rationale: glossary sentence contradicts ADR-1005 text; derived I8/E3 = LOW per architect; reporter's native SHOULD disagreed, derived band governs

trigger: operator registers an element with a wrong address or credential
summary: No element reachability/state model: `state` is unenumerated, no test-connection step, no per-element reachability signal (stream_up is core→gnmic only), so 'registered' and 'reachable' look identical. Fix: enumerate state (incl. no_profile), name the signal driving last_seen, specify or explicitly defer test-connection.
classification_rationale: normal workflow step with no owner in a binding ADR

trigger: any host behind a multi-tier fabric in steady state (MAC present in access, distribution and core switch FDBs)
summary: Attachment join returns every element whose FDB holds the MAC; no edge-port rule (port with no LLDP neighbour, MAC-count), no result shape for multiple matches / none / in-purview-without-Incident (whole-call deny vs per-row omission). 'Attached to switch X port 12' would be presented as correct when it is a trunk. Fix: edge-port rule + matches[] with role + none/denied shapes.
classification_rationale: result shape unspecified; the wrong answer is presented as correct (I3)

trigger: any get_network_element_state call
summary: 'typed output schema' over vendor-variable OpenConfig payloads is an envelope + open JSON and the ADR does not admit it; empty-cache (just-registered) vs constrained unspecified; D10 'allowlist is the subscription list' conflicts with D11 vendor profiles mapping facts to per-vendor paths (which table drives subscriptions?).
classification_rationale: A5 claim not honestly specified (I6); recorder's derivation: reporter also listed I3 for the empty-cache case, which is UP-4's finding and gates there — not retained here

trigger: alert/dashboard on a series lacking element_name (gnmic_* target-health metrics; rename label churn)
summary: Whether gnmic's own gnmic_* target-health metrics carry event-tags is unstated and unverified; a rename creates new series; no lookup path for on-call stated. Fix: state the guarantee per series class or document ne- id resolution via get_network_element.
classification_rationale: speculative — reporter did not verify gnmic's label behaviour on internal metrics; mandatory investigation at NICE band

trigger: any read made under an Incident
summary: How a read binds to its Incident (parameter/header/session) is neither specified nor in the Open list; derived-purview evaluation timing vs 0068's never-stored read-time join (an unresolved MAC makes purview undecidable → fail-closed) unstated. Fix: add both to Open.
classification_rationale: stub's Open list omits two mechanism questions its fixed semantics depend on

trigger: agentic worker retries register_network_element with the same management address
summary: idempotentHint: true asserted for registration tools, but id is core-minted and address is a mutable attribute, so a retry mints a second element/credential/gnmic target (two device sessions, double observations). No natural key or conflict-vs-same-id contract; credential rotation mid-poll and republish semantics unstated. Fix: define upsert on (address, adapter) or set idempotentHint:false and state behaviour.
classification_rationale: false safe-direction A5 hint = I4 per docs/agentic-first-principle.md §A5

trigger: admin grants NetworkEngineer via the fleet-wide assign route
summary: kRbacAssignableRoles (rbac_assignable_roles.hpp:54) is a closed six-role list with an MCP schema enum and a kRbacSecurables mirror in mcp_server.cpp; the ADR seeds NetworkEngineer without naming these, so the role is unassignable as designed. Fix: Consequences item — add to the list, enum, mirror and sync test.
classification_rationale: required consequence omitted; verified against the header

trigger: fresh install with the compose service
summary: Bootstrap order (core up → collector principal created by whom → token minted/mounted → gnmic start), gnmic behaviour on 401/empty list at first boot, and how core learns the gnmic endpoint + client mTLS material (flag names) are unspecified and not deferred.
classification_rationale: deployment workflow unowned; deferred-to-slice acceptable if said

trigger: upgrade where no element is ever registered
summary: ADR never states the surfaces and securable seed are additive, that the FencedLeaderOnly subscriber is structurally dormant with no collector endpoint configured, or that stream_up==0 cannot fire for non-users (distinct from arch-2).

trigger: normal operation over weeks; disable/delete of an element
summary: No aging/pruning/retention for FDB/ARP observations (unbounded growth; clock-guarded-retention routed row applies to any future pass and is not named); disable/delete effects on loader target, stored rows and gnmic cache unspecified.
classification_rationale: retention obligation unstated — I5 base MEDIUM, no raise (not a serialised security path). Recorder's derivation: reporter also listed I2 for 'dangling rows'; orphaned rows are not destruction or corruption of data, so I2 is not retained

trigger: SecretCodec decrypt fails for 1 of N targets during gnmic's 60s poll (KEK retirement window, orphaned/tampered blob)
summary: One bad credential row takes one element dark silently: a route that omits the row and returns 200 triggers gnmic on-delete (session torn down, stream_up stays 1, only last_seen stalls). Fix D6: a per-target decrypt failure 500s the whole fetch (gnmic retains the prior list) + fetch_failed_total{reason} + alert.
classification_rationale: ADR silent on partial decrypt failure (overlaps sec-7's list; kept because it names the gnmic on-delete consequence)

trigger: N consecutive collector-targets fetch failures (401 after token rotation, core down)
summary: gnmic's behaviour on loader fetch error (retain last list / empty / drop) is assumed, not stated; a stale list runs stale credentials indefinitely with only per-replica last_fetch_seconds showing it. MANDATORY INVESTIGATION: verify gnmic's loader error path, then state it in D6 and bind the alert to leader-emitted last_fetch_seconds.
classification_rationale: security-relevant omission (I7 raise) — speculative on gnmic's loader behaviour, so a mandatory investigation at the derived band, not a merge blocker until resolved

trigger: blue/green or copied compose pointing a second gnmic at core
summary: Two collectors on one principal: indistinguishable in the fetch audit, 2x device load, duplicate series. Fix: one collector principal per collector; a second source for one principal within an interval alerts (defines the 'unexpected source' alert).

trigger: gnmic restart (cold cache) or cache expiration evicting an unchanged ON_CHANGE leaf
summary: Absent-vs-empty on cache Get: an empty subtree is read by a worker as 'no interfaces / no FDB entries'. Fix D10: empty cache = constrained: no_data_yet (stream healthy) or constrained: stale (restart/eviction), never an empty table; verify whether gnmic's gNMI-server cache honours expiration and set it explicitly.
classification_rationale: project cornerstone (absent-not-zero) violated by silence; wrong result presented as correct

trigger: device unreachable / cert expired / gnmic→device session dropped while core↔gnmic stream stays up
summary: 'Observable, never silent' covers the core↔gnmic hop only: under ON_CHANGE a quiet healthy switch and a dead one both leave last_seen static with stream_up=1 — false assurance. Fix D9: name the per-target liveness source (SAMPLE heartbeat path per target, or gnmic's target-state metric) and define last_seen as advancing on that only; qualify stream_up as the core↔gnmic hop.
classification_rationale: I6(a) false assurance: the ADR advertises an observability control that does not hold for the device hop

trigger: leadership handover mid-notification
summary: Fenced-out batch and non-atomic batch: ADR says the ex-leader 'cannot write', not what happens to the batch or whether edges+observations are one txn; a split write mixes epochs. Fix D9: one txn per batch, first data statement READ COMMITTED (leader_elector.hpp:153-158), fenced-out batch dropped + counted, new leader's initial sync is the recovery.
classification_rationale: ADR silent on batch atomicity and fenced-out disposition. Recorder's derivation: reporter listed I2; the new leader's initial sync re-establishes state so nothing is destroyed — not retained; I7 (required contract text missing) is the operative impact

trigger: a core switch's 50k-row FDB arrives in one notification; core consumes slowly
summary: One upsert exceeds statement_timeout_ms=30000 (pg_pool.hpp:89) → batch fails forever for the largest switches while stream_up=1; the lease held meanwhile starves heartbeat ingest and is_revoked() on the shared ADR-0012 PgPool; a slow consumer makes gnmic drop ON_CHANGE updates → permanent divergence until resubscribe. I5(b) raise: serialised path shared with a security operation. Fix D9: chunked bounded writes, a bounded lease-hold budget separate from request traffic, periodic full resync.
classification_rationale: ADR silent; I5 raised to HIGH under clause (b)

trigger: gNMI delete notification for a removed LLDP neighbour; switch RMA (same IP, new chassis-id, same ne-uuid); element disabled/deregistered
summary: Edges never retire; two physical devices' edges merge under one id; the service diagram draws yesterday's fabric as current. Fix D7: delete notification retires the edge (last_seen frozen, retired_at set); chassis-id/serial change = audited identity_change, prior edges retired, operator chooses relabel-vs-new; disable retires edges.
classification_rationale: ADR silent on edge retirement and identity change; wrong result presented as correct

trigger: a laptop moves ports within one sync window
summary: Read-time join returns two attachments with overlapping windows; a tool that picks one presents a guess as fact. Fix D7/D10: attachments return every candidate with both windows and ambiguous:true, never a single pick. (Companion to hp-2, which is the steady-state multi-tier case.)
classification_rationale: result shape for overlapping observations unspecified; I3/E3 derives HIGH (reporter's native MEDIUM disagreed; derived band governs). Fixed together with hp-2's shape rule

trigger: a management group is declared in-purview, or a device moves into one, after the element's purview was derived
summary: Stale element purview: the element's FDB/ARP tables disclose an in-purview person's presence without an Incident; no re-derivation cadence stated. Fix 0067 D1/D7: derivation evaluated at read time against current membership (no cached verdict), or re-derived on every purview/membership write with the old verdict invalidated.

trigger: the FDB join surface (arch-3) is absent or its store degrades
summary: Fail-closed derivation has no stated scope: if 'cannot determine' is fleet-wide, every element's tables are denied to everyone on a Postgres hiccup. Fix 0067 D7: fail-closed is per subject; determinable subjects unaffected; the denial is counted and alerted.
classification_rationale: ADR silent on the scope of fail-closed

trigger: approver deprovisioned (ADR-2001 revoke); TTL lapse mid-request; audit persist failure under an open Incident
summary: Incident edge cases are listed as OPEN (deferred-to-mechanism acceptable) if D6 adds now: 'audit-persist failure denies the read even under an Incident — an unrecordable read is not made'.
classification_rationale: deferred-to-mechanism acceptable with one sentence now; I7/E3 derives MEDIUM (reporter's native LOW-as-deferred disagreed; derived band governs)

trigger: an NX-OS/Junos profile maps /lldp to a vendor-native path
summary: D10 OpenConfig-path allowlist vs D11 vendor-native subscriptions: either native paths are cached and an OC Get returns empty (UP-4's I3) or they are excluded (feature unreachable). Fix D10: allowlist keyed by canonical fact; profile expands fact→vendor path at both subscription publish and Get shape check; Get by vendor path refused. (Companion to hp-3/sec-4 last clause — this is the vendor-path half.)
classification_rationale: I3/E3 derives HIGH (reporter's native MEDIUM disagreed; derived band governs). Fixed together with sec-4/hp-3's allowlist-vs-profile rule

trigger: gnmic image digest bump changes loader JSON shape or source label semantics
summary: No contract test against the pinned image (loader shape, cache Get, label names) named for a pin change. Fix D11: name it; deferred-to-slice acceptable if said.

trigger: ordinary operation (every MAC ever seen, forever)
summary: Observations are an unbounded presence log with no retention; GDPR storage-limitation exposure; a closed Incident deletes nothing. Fix D7: observations retention window distinct from edges, adopting the clock-guarded-retention apparatus (PG shared-row variant), and Incident closure does not purge history. (Same defect as hp-10's first half — independently raised in the same wave.)
classification_rationale: ADR silent; routed clock-guarded-retention row binds any future prune

trigger: gnmic restart or core↔gnmic TCP loss
summary: retry_after_ms is derived from a 'reconnect backoff' the ADR never defines; a resubscribe's initial sync is not declared the authority for retiring absent edges. Fix D9: jittered exponential backoff with cap; initial sync is a full snapshot that retires edges not present.
classification_rationale: Recorder's derivation: reporter listed I7, but the backoff is implementation detail, not one of the six required-doc items — I8 is the operative impact

trigger: implementation slice adds the NetworkElement securable / Collect operation without the mirrors
summary: Collect is a precedented non-CRUD op (Push/Attest/Rotate) but every closed list it must join is unnamed: ops[] rbac_store.cpp:698, kRbacOps mcp_server.cpp:4166, kSeededOperations test_capability_catalogue.cpp:113, types[]/kRbacSecurables/kSeededSecurableTypes, test_rbac_store binding test, rbac.md:348/447 tables, the '38 securable types' counts. Truth mismatch: D5 'Read+Write to Administrator' vs the Administrator loop (rbac_store.cpp:768) granting all CRUD ops on every seeded type — state whether NetworkElement joins the loop.
classification_rationale: item 5 (permission table); role list is hp-7

trigger: ADR-0067 derives the gate set from the funnel's callers; the most sensitive caller has no verb
summary: Only network_element.state.view is named. Unnamed audit verbs: list_network_element_attachments (the one read 0067 purview-gates), the collector-targets fetch, registration/credential/purview-override/profile-override writes, Incident open/approve/close.

trigger: alert-group change authored against D8
summary: Metric-name parity: observability-conventions.md:8 mandates yuzu_server_* for server metrics, fleet rollups are yuzu_fleet_*; yuzu_network_elements_by_* matches neither; ..._collector_last_fetch_seconds is undecidable age-vs-epoch vs shipped shapes; the collector-principal fetch counter D6's alert depends on is unnamed and needs a bounded source dimension (a peer-address label violates label discipline).

trigger: implementation lands collector-targets with no twin and no ledger entry
summary: Write tools unnamed/uncounted (D7 implies register, credentials, enabled, purview override, profile override) with no REST paths — parity uncheckable; GET collector-targets is REST-only by design but not recorded in ADR-1005's dated exception ledger (SCIM :132, erasure :169, chunked-receive :207 all are).

trigger: mechanism design reads the glossary as canonical
summary: 0067:16-17 declares the CONTEXT glossary canonical, yet CONTEXT's Purview enforcement sentence omits D7's fail-closed clause — the security clause lives only in the non-canonical home.

trigger: PR merges with no changelog fragment
summary: Rule 3 exempts refactors/CI/test-only, not docs-only ADRs; practice contradicts Gate 1's exemption (design-only ADR PRs shipped fragments: 2080, 2090, 2142, 2365); the roadmap status flips to settled. Policy-floor candidate ('missing mandated fragment') for the orchestrator to adjudicate.
classification_rationale: item 3 — orchestrator disposition: fragment added in the hardening round (precedent governs), so no floor adjudication needed

trigger: N consecutive collector-targets fetch failures (401 after token rotation, core down)
summary: Investigation resolved from the loader source (openconfig/gnmic pkg/loaders/http_loader/http_loader.go, read 2026-10-04): update() logs the fetch error and returns before updateTargets(), so lastTargets is unchanged and no delete op is emitted; a SUCCESSFUL response omitting a target goes through Diff() → delete + OnDelete. No retry/backoff beyond the fixed interval. Finding stands at HIGH as a required security-relevant statement for D6; no longer speculative.
classification_rationale: resolution of the mandatory investigation; band unchanged (not a de-escalation)

trigger: FDB/ARP rows stored with first_seen/last_seen for every device on every switch, including visitors' phones and guest VLANs
summary: Data classification understated and deferred: 'same device-CI tier' — but device_ci is current-state one-row-per-agent, while observations are a time-series presence log over non-agent and non-employee MACs, exactly the presence/working-hours proxy the SOC 2 doc treats as co-determination-relevant for netconn (which is off by default). Tier determines controls, so it must be decided in the ADR: new category (presence/location-over-time), behavioural-adjacent, works-council-relevant, personal data where MAC→person resolvable; edges are asset topology; lawful basis for non-employee MACs, default retention and the collection posture decided before slice 1; rows forward-declared in the SOC 2 inventory now.
classification_rationale: tier claim weaker than the SOC 2 doc's own reasoning for comparable data

trigger: a MAC resolves to a person via device_ci → agent → user, or a visitor DSAR
summary: No retention, DSAR or erasure statement for an identifying store (UP-15/hp-10 cover retention only): the store must be named an erasure source, the AgentDecommission cascade (SOC 2 :417) extended to it, and 'Incident closure does not purge history' bounded — observations keep a retention window independent of any Incident; rows tied to an exported Incident held only until the export's own retention expires; retention row added to clock-guarded-retention.md's adoption register. I7 raised: omission conceals a legal-exposure/data-loss risk.

trigger: an auditor or works council requests the 'complete exportable account'
summary: Incident evidence promise has no named rows: opening justification, approval row (requester/approver/distinct human roots per ADR-0033 §4), expiry/closure, denials during the window, purview-flag/override changes — no verbs, no retention (audit store 365d), no tamper-evidence. I6(a) false assurance: an advertised evidence control not enforced. Fix: verbs incident.open/.approve/.deny/.close/.expire, purview.set/.override; every read carries incident_id; export generated from audit rows only, retained ≥365d, its generation audited with a content hash.
classification_rationale: item 5; overlaps sec-6/C-2/UP-12 but this is the CC7.2 evidence-chain angle

trigger: an operator reads /interfaces or /lldp (asset topology) and /fdb or /neighbors (presence) under the same verb
summary: One verb network_element.state.view conflates non-personal topology reads with presence reads, breaking works-council countability (the Device-pages row's device.live.<kind> rule). Fix: split — state.view (topology/inventory, not behavioural), presence.view (FDB/ARP/neighbours via emit_behavioral_audit), a third verb for the attachment join; names into audit-log.md. Derived I3/E3 = HIGH; reporter's native MEDIUM disagreed, derived band governs.

trigger: the collector token leaks
summary: 'Accepted residual risk' in an ADR is not the SOC 2 doc's risk-register posture (precedent :561: entry with mitigations and an owner). Fix: risk-register entry with owner, review cadence, bearer lifetime/rotation (sec-7); the 'unexpected source' alert is a control needing a bounded source dimension (C-3/UP-3); name the real inventory sections. Recorder's derivation: reporter listed I1 ('acceptance is not a control'); no control fails by the omission — the missing artefact is the register entry (I7).

trigger: implementer looks for the named inventories
summary: ADR cites a 'what can read a secret' inventory and an 'individual behavioural read' inventory by name; neither exists in the SOC 2 doc (grep 0 hits). Name the real sections: the stores table (:389-433) and the behavioural-channels list (:553-560).
classification_rationale: cited artefacts do not exist by those names

trigger: attachment join on an unresolvable MAC
summary: State that an unresolved MAC is returned as 'unresolved' and that the join exposes MAC→person only when the caller may read both sides (links hp-2/arch-3).

trigger: CC8.1 trace of the verdict
summary: Appendix row and roadmap banner record the verdict by name and date only; add 'tracking: PR #5367'. Not required for validity (the 2026-07-14 precedent cites no issue), but cheap.

trigger: Postgres pool-acquire timeout, query error or SecretCodec decrypt failure while serving collector-targets
summary: Loader route degrade behaviour unspecified: an implementer degrading to {} or a partial map makes gnmic drop every target via on-delete (collection stops fleet-wide; empty list reads as 'no elements'). Same class as the app-usage '503-on-degrade never empty-200' rule. Fix D6: all-or-503 with retry hint, never empty/partial 200; core authoritative, gnmic converges to the last successful response. (gnmic retains its last list on a 5xx — UP-2 verified.) Derived HIGH; reporter's native MEDIUM disagreed.
classification_rationale: routed precedent (app-usage row) names the rule; ADR silent

trigger: implementer wires NetworkElementStore into /readyz stores_ok or makes gnmic reachability a readiness dependency
summary: /readyz answer unstated: gnmic endpoint/stream/fetch state must never be readiness inputs (ADR-1005:83 names engines; gnmic is not one by name, so the ADR must say it); whether NetworkElementStore joins stores_ok must be stated; a store degrade counts + 503s the routes, never pulls the replica.

trigger: a device-reported free-text vendor string becomes a metric label (D7 'vendor/model/OS as learned' drives yuzu_network_elements_by_vendor)
summary: vendor label cardinality unbounded as written. Fix D8: vendor = profile family (closed set from content/network-profiles/ + unknown), state/adapter closed enums, learned strings row-only, label sets from a constexpr list.
classification_rationale: label discipline vs the learned-string source

trigger: alert-group author works from D8
summary: The promised 'alert on fetches from an unexpected source' is unmeasurable with D8's metrics (per-source = peer IP, unbounded); the OTA precedent defers thresholds, not contracts — the ADR names the group but no alert names/signals. Fix D8: name NetworkCollectorStreamDown (stream_up==0), NetworkCollectorFetchStale (last_fetch), NetworkCollectorFetchRejected (counter{result}), NetworkCollectorTargetDown (up{job=gnmic}); 'unexpected source' is an audit-row signal or a bounded result=denied counter; gnmic expiration must exceed the scrape interval by a margin.
classification_rationale: item 6 (observability row): alert contract names required now, thresholds deferred

trigger: D11 implemented as cited
summary: Compose healthcheck gate covers the five Yuzu images + postgres (ci-architecture.md:367-382) and check-compose-versions.sh matches only ghcr.io/<owner>/yuzu-{server,gateway,agent} — neither touches ghcr.io/openconfig/gnmic, so 'added to FILES' is a no-op and the pin has no mechanical guard; D3 disables gnmic's API server (/healthz) so the probe target is unnamed. Fix: probe = TCP/HTTP against gnmic's Prometheus listener with a tool verified in the image; pin guarded by a dedicated check or the UP-14 contract test; scrape job in all four deploy/prometheus files; name which compose files carry the service.
classification_rationale: cited gates do not cover this image

trigger: Postgres restored to an older snapshot; gnmic volume lost; KEK lost
summary: Recovery/restore semantics absent: after a restore the next poll deletes later-registered elements from gnmic with no store row to explain it (correct convergence, unstated); gnmic holds no durable state; KEK loss makes credentials unrecoverable (ADR-0010) → re-enter; backup scope. Fix: Consequences states 'core authoritative, gnmic converges' + runbook in docs/user-manual/server-admin.md.
classification_rationale: item 2 (operator workflow) + the promised data-inventory row

trigger: N=5000 elements at the 60s loader interval (+1 audit row per fetch)
summary: Poll cost and N unbounded (≈2 MB body, 5000 decrypts well under a second — not hot, but competes with the pool). Fix D6: supported-scale bound, interval knob with floor, ETag/If-None-Match → 304 for an unchanged list, unchanged-poll audit coalesced.

trigger: a pilot network team asks for firewall rules
summary: No network-flow statement and no deferral: loader direction/port (gnmic→core HTTPS), gNMI-server port (core→gnmic), gnmic→device gNMI port (vendor-variable 57400/6030/9339), Prometheus→gnmic scrape, management VRF/zone placement all unstated. Fix D11: a flow table (source, destination, port, protocol, auth, direction) + 'full guidance ships in server-admin.md with slice 1'.

trigger: a security questionnaire asks about device-credential storage/rotation and PKI
summary: Partly answerable: device mTLS with customer PKI is accurate, but cert rotation on the gnmic side (tls-reload — unverified), provenance/rotation of the core↔gnmic mTLS pair and the CA gnmic trusts for the loader, the operator procedure to rotate a device password and its propagation (60s), and a tracking issue for reference mode are all unstated. Fix: a 'Questionnaire answers' block in Consequences naming the CAIQ/shared-responsibility rows (SOC 2 :617-621): Yuzu = control plane; customer = gnmic hosting, device certs, device-side AAA.

trigger: operator runs docker compose up on the shipped file after upgrade
summary: Compose placement/opt-in unstated (docker-compose.yml today: server, postgres, prometheus, grafana — verified). Fix D11: yuzu-netcollector is an opt-in profile/overlay absent from default up; default behaviour unchanged on upgrade; making it default later = Breaking fragment; name an install path for non-compose banks (Podman/systemd/VM). Precedent: SOC 2 :483 treats a separately-deployed opt-in artifact as the collection off-switch.
classification_rationale: item 2 (upgrade note) — concealed-breaking-change risk if unconditional

trigger: a bank mirrors registries / scans third-party images
summary: Third-party posture partly undocumented: precedent = tag+sha256 digest pin (Prometheus/Grafana), dependabot docker ecosystem on /deploy/docker tracks it; no SBOM/NOTICE requirement by precedent (NICE). Missing: digest-mirror statement (content-addressed survives a by-digest mirror; tag-only mirror behaviour), vuln-scan ownership (customer scans; Yuzu's release SBOM excludes it), who watches the gnmic CVE feed, and 'separate process, Apache-2.0, no linking' for licence clarity.

trigger: a German bank evaluates the works-council posture
summary: ADR-0067 says it 'generalises' the SOC 2 doc's named works-council gaps (:564) but never enumerates which it closes (partially: drill-down kill switch, per-group toggle) vs stays open (pseudonymisation, retention UI, DEX:Read, DSAR); ADR-0068 opens a NEW unnamed per-category collection gap (FDB/ARP observations with no collection toggle); the default-out posture is acceptable only once the EU flip exists, which is wholly open — EU deployments must not enable the collector before the flip ships. Fix: closes/stays-open table; cite the opt-in-artifact precedent (:483) as the collection off-switch.
classification_rationale: item 2 + SOC 2 gap list; not legal advice

trigger: a pilot on a Cisco campus estate registers a Catalyst IOS-XE element
